policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'nor of uncleanness' renders either negative conjunction identically; oude/oute is not distinguished in English and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'approved of God' carries no marker for the Greek article; the presence or absence of to before theo leaves the English identical.
ASV 'were we found using words of flattery' renders the bare dative and the en phrase alike; the preposition leaves no trace in the English.
ASV text reads 'we were gentle in the midst of you' = epioi; the marginal note 'Most of the ancient authorities read babes' assigns nepioi to the margin, not to the text.
ASV 'as when a nurse cherisheth' renders hos ean and hos an the same way; the particle is not distinguished in English.
ASV 'ye were become very dear to us' is an archaic past that fits the aorist egenethete and the perfect gegenesthe alike; no note is mapped here.

ASV has a single 'For' opening the verse (for the gar of 'For ye remember') and none before 'working night and day'; the added gar of the longer reading would supply that second connective, which the ASV does not render.
ASV 'that ye should walk worthily' does not distinguish present from aorist infinitive; the verse's textual note concerns 'calleth/called' (the participle), not this lemma.
ASV opens the verse 'And for this cause we also thank God', rendering the leading Kai; the separate 'also' answers kai hemeis, so the initial conjunction is present in the English.
A transposition of alethos and estin; ASV 'as it is in truth' is compatible with either order and the note here is a Greek gloss on 'word of hearing'.
ASV reads 'the Lord Jesus and the prophets' with no possessive; the longer reading's idious would surface as 'their own prophets', which the ASV does not have.
ASV reads 'but the wrath is come upon them' with no genitive qualifier; the longer reading's tou theou would surface as 'the wrath of God', which the ASV does not have.
ASV renders 'because we would fain have come unto you', a causal clause answering dioti; the inferential dio would give 'wherefore', which the ASV does not read.
